avoid_supplements.name: Warfarin/Anticoagulants
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Mefenamic acid increases bleeding risk by inhibiting platelet function and displacing warfarin from protein binding, elevating INR
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid concurrent use; if necessary, monitor INR closely with frequent testing and dose adjustment

avoid_supplements.name: High-dose Aspirin
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Combined NSAID use increases GI bleeding, ulceration, and cardiovascular event risk
avoid_supplements.action: Do not combine; use only one NSAID at a time

avoid_supplements.name: Lithium
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Mefenamic acid reduces renal lithium clearance, increasing serum levels to toxic concentrations
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid combination; if necessary, monitor serum lithium levels and renal function weekly

avoid_supplements.name: ACE Inhibitors/Angiotensin II Receptor Blockers
avoid_supplements.mechanism: NSAIDs reduce the antihypertensive effect and increase risk of acute kidney injury and hyperkalemia
avoid_supplements.action: Monitor blood pressure and serum creatinine; consider alternative pain management

avoid_supplements.name: Methotrexate
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Mefenamic acid decreases methotrexate renal clearance, increasing toxicity risk
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid; use alternative analgesic if pain management needed during methotrexate therapy

caution_supplements.name: Fish Oil/Omega-3 Fatty Acids
caution_supplements.mechanism: May have additive antiplatelet effects with mefenamic acid, slightly increasing bleeding risk
caution_supplements.action: Monitor for unusual bruising or bleeding; use lowest effective doses

caution_supplements.name: Ginger
caution_supplements.mechanism: Potential additive antiplatelet and anticoagulant properties with NSAIDs
caution_supplements.action: Monitor for signs of bleeding; inform provider if using high-dose ginger supplements

caution_supplements.name: Garlic Supplements
caution_supplements.mechanism: May have mild antiplatelet effects that could potentiate bleeding risk
caution_supplements.action: Use moderate amounts; counsel on signs of excessive bleeding

avoid_foods.name: Alcohol (>2 drinks daily)
avoid_foods.mechanism: Significantly increases GI bleeding and ulceration risk; alcohol also increases hepatotoxicity
avoid_foods.action: Counsel to minimize or eliminate alcohol consumption during mefenamic acid therapy

caution_foods.name: High-fat meals
caution_foods.mechanism: May delay and enhance mefenamic acid absorption, potentially increasing GI side effects
caution_foods.action: Take mefenamic acid with food or milk to reduce GI irritation; avoid large fatty meals before dosing

caution_foods.name: Caffeine-containing beverages
caution_foods.mechanism: Mild additive GI irritation; may increase gastric acidity
caution_foods.action: Limit coffee, tea, and cola consumption; take medication with non-acidic beverage

monitoring_notes: Monitor renal function (serum creatinine, BUN) and electrolytes (especially potassium) at baseline and periodically during use. Assess for signs of GI bleeding, edema, hypertension, and cardiovascular events. Counsel patients on appropriate duration of use (typically ≤7 days) and to report persistent abdominal pain, black stools, or unusual bleeding.
